reachability: Every new life is made at Yale in New Haven at one of five US banks (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Citi, Capital One), and since the scope reset of 2026-10-09 nothing moves a life. Creation's Before Yale can keep a home-country account at a bank abroad where its terms allow (systems/homeaccount.ts), so a played life can hold an account at a British, French, German, Spanish, Irish, Icelandic, Canadian, Mexican, Japanese, Korean, Australian or New Zealand bank beside the American one. items.item: A bank closing an idle German account at zero (closedByBank and the dormancy/idle path): it can go negative from fees on closing; make the bank's own close settle consistently; closure can't erase debt or strand money; closed accounts stop all recurring processing.
items.requirement: BGB § 675h(2): a payment service provider ends a framework contract on at least two months' notice; § 675h(3): on termination, regularly charged fees are owed pro rata up to the end of the contract (dejure.org text, read 2026-10-16; gesetze-im-internet.de refused the fetch with 503). So fees accrued to the closing are owed, not forgiven, and a balance can't be manufactured where there is none to take them from. The project's own rule (CLAUDE.md, the ledger law; brief section 7): every movement a balanced posting, funds never vanish or duplicate, a closure can't strand money or erase a debt. SLATE's existing rule for a customer's close (bankmoves.ts closeRefusal:282-307, accountlife.ts cancelRefusal:237-261): the bank closes an overdrawn account only once that's paid.
items.currentBehavior: No German bank reaches the bank's own close at zero: closedByBank (bankmoves.ts:333-340) runs only from the day's check at bankmoves.ts:420-438, which reads OPENING (content/bankopening.ts:44-84), and only Citi (closesAtZeroAfterDays 90) and Capital One (fundWithinDays 60) carry those rules. Germany has no unclaimed-money law (content/accountlife.ts UNCLAIMED.DE has no years), so idleAccounts (accountlife.ts:609-646) never closes a German account, and dormancy (accountlife.ts:616-619) blocks without closing. So the defect named is latent: closedByBank checks `balance !== 0` before closeNow (bankmoves.ts:310-326), which then settles interest (settleInterest, banking.ts:508) and fees (settleFees, banking.ts:492-500, Germany's quarter only); with no remainderTo, interest settled would stay on a closed account (stranded), and fees would leave a closed account negative with nothing pursuing it (leftOverdrawn, lending.ts:937-953, skips closed accounts). Reproduced only with a bank given a zero-close rule in a test (TEST SETUP). The German bank's own close that does happen is the overdraft's (closeForOverdraft, lending.ts:955-1054): reproduced on a Berlin quickSave (probe, Commerzbank primary, a Deutsche Bank AktivKonto €100 under from 5 January 2026): charged off on 7 March at €101.97 with feesDue €13.80 (January's and February's €6.90) left on the closed account and never charged, and March's fee and the overdraft interest built since 1 March (odAccrued) dropped too. Played the same way at a home account abroad (a German home bank's AktivKonto emptied to Chase, its €6.90 overdrawing it).

items.plan: closedByBank: work out what closing would settle (interest net of tax, the fees closing charges, the overdraft interest built) before closing; close only where that leaves nothing owed, and send anything it leaves (interest) to the current account kept elsewhere by the bank's own payment, never stranded; where closing would leave it owing, don't close: the charges post at their regular closing and the account is pursued as any overdrawn one (the 60 days, closeForOverdraft), as the customer's Close It refuses it. closeForOverdraft: settle the overdraft interest built and, on each account it closes, Germany's quarter of fees before the set-off, so they're set off or charged off with the rest, never dropped; the quiet re-banking after a charge-off doesn't settle them a second time or move a negative to the new bank. Scheduled payments and standing orders into an account it closes dropped (dropPaymentsFor), as every other close does. Recurring processing on a closed account checked one by one (interest, fees, the abroad fee, statements, round-ups, alerts, standing orders) and tested.

PLAYER JOURNEY, New Haven: Capital One's 360 Checking closed unfunded and a Citi account charged off: after the close, months on the clock post nothing to the closed account, no statement, no alert, no round-up, no fee, no interest; across a reload. items.plan: A one-time step on opening (`findTermInterest`, named in SaveUniverse.opened): for each open term deposit still in its cooling-off, its bank letting interest be taken during the term, the untagged “Interest: <name>” transactions into its holder's account from its opening on are the candidates; the term's own accrual is replayed day end by day end from its opening (its balance × its rate / 365, each candidate taken where it equals the whole cents built then), and only a set of candidates that reproduces the term's stored accrued exactly is taken as its own, the earliest where two fit, and none taken by another term. Recorded on the term as the transactions' ids; interestPaidSince reads them beside the tag. Where no set fits, nothing is attributed: the interest stays as the build that paid it left it (that build never returned it), never taken back from a term that may not have paid it.
